title: Adaptive Sampling of Coastal Sensor Networks Under Intermittent Connectivity

headings.text: Adaptive Sampling of Coastal Sensor Networks Under Intermittent Connectivity

key_sentences: Coastal sensor networks lose connectivity whenever a storm or a tide interrupts the radio link.
We present a sampling scheme that adapts the measurement rate to the expected length of the outage.
A reading that cannot be sent must be stored, and storage on a small node is limited.
The tidal component is predicted from the published tide table, so no training data is needed.
The adaptive scheme loses the fewest readings while its energy use stays close to that of the slow fixed scheme.
The deployment covered 40 nodes on 12 piers and 8 buoys between April and September.
Adapting the sampling rate to the predicted outage length reduces data loss without a measurable cost in latency.

tables.caption: Table 1. Loss, energy and delay of three sampling schemes

list_items.text: (i) a compact model of outage length based on the tide table;
(ii) a rate controller that needs no tuning on the node;
(iii) a field evaluation over six months on 40 nodes.
[1] Okafor, L., and Brandt, T. (2021). Duty cycling in tidal radio links. Journal of Sensor Systems, 9(2), 101–118.
[2] Lindqvist, S. (2019). Buffer management on constrained nodes. Proceedings of the Workshop on Ocean Observation, 44–51.
[3] Mendes, R., et al. (2022). Predicting outage lengths from tide tables. Marine Technology Letters, 14(1), 22–30.
[4] Tanaka, H. (2020). Energy accounting for battery-powered buoys. Sensors and Actuators in the Sea, 5(4), 301–315.
